Container.Name: nextime
Container.Overview: A calendar for families and small groups on your own server. One container, SQLite, and a calm look of its own. Own calendars with colors and symbols sit next to iCloud, Google and other CalDAV calendars such as Nextcloud, read and written and synced every minute, plus subscriptions and built-in public and school holidays. Today, day, week and month show what comes next; events have reminders, a place with a small map, attachments and repeats, and quick entry turns one line into an event. Calendars are shared with other accounts (busy only, read or edit) or with guests through a link. A CalDAV server under /dav/ brings your calendars to Apple Calendar, DAVx5 on Android and Thunderbird, with a password per device and a QR code for the iPhone (needs https). Due tasks from nextasks and deadlines from nexpaper can show in the calendar. nextime installs from the browser as an app, speaks English and German, and has a REST API and an MCP server. Accounts come by invitation, with a second factor (TOTP) and sign-in through OpenID Connect providers. Backups run every night and can be downloaded and restored. This is an early release: keep a backup and open an issue when something is wrong.
Container.Description: A calendar for families and small groups on your own server: own and shared calendars, iCloud, Google and CalDAV in one place, and a CalDAV server for iPhone and Android. Open the WebUI and create the first account; it becomes the operator. It needs the setup code from the container log (click the nextime icon, then Logs), a new one at every start until nextime is set up. To choose the code yourself, set Setup Code below. Further accounts come by invitation. Phones and other calendar programs connect only over https: put nextime behind a reverse proxy with TLS, then set Public URL and Trusted Proxies. All data lives under /data: the SQLite database, attachments, secret.key, backups, logs and your own languages. Keep it on a local disk, never on an SMB or NFS share, because SQLite locking is not reliable over network filesystems. nextime makes its own backup every night at 03:00 in the server's time zone. Set PUID and PGID to the user that should own the files. 99 and 100 are the Unraid defaults and work out of the box.

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Port you reach nextime at. Container port: 8000

Config.Name: Data (Container Path: /data)
Config.Description: Holds the SQLite database, attachments, the key secret.key, backups, logs and your own languages. Keep it on a local disk, not on a network share.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User id that should own the files in /data. 99 is the Unraid default.

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group id that should own the files in /data. 100 is the Unraid default.

Config.Name: Time Zone
Config.Description: The server's time zone, for example Europe/Berlin: the nightly backup runs at 03:00 in it. Each account chooses its own time zone in the interface. Leave blank for UTC.

Config.Name: Setup Code
Config.Description: The code the first account needs to become the operator. Leave blank: nextime makes a new one at every start until it is set up and writes it to the container log.

Config.Name: Public URL
Config.Description: The address people use to reach nextime, for example https://calendar.example.com when it sits behind a reverse proxy. Used for invitation links, guest links and the return address of OpenID Connect and Google. Leave blank to take the address of the request; the setting in the interface wins when set.

Config.Name: Trusted Proxies
Config.Description: Addresses or networks of your reverse proxies, comma separated, for example 172.16.0.0/12. Only their X-Forwarded-For and X-Forwarded-Proto are believed, so only they can tell nextime that a request came in over https (phones need that); without it every sign-in seems to come from the proxy and the brake against password guessing cannot tell people apart.

Config.Name: Container Port (host networking only)
Config.Description: Leave this empty unless you switched Network Type to Host. In bridge mode the WebUI Port above already does the job and setting this will break it, because the mapping still points at 8000. On host networking the port inside the container is the port on your server, so use this to move nextime off 8000 if something else is already there.

Config.Name: Secret Key
Config.Description: Protects the server-side secrets (the passwords of iCloud and other calendar accounts, the client secrets of sign-in providers, the mail password, the seeds of second factors). Leave blank: nextime creates one on first start and keeps it in /data/secret.key.

Config.Name: Places URL
Config.Description: The address search behind the suggestions in the place field, a Photon service. Leave blank for the free one at photon.komoot.io. nextime asks it, not the browser, and sends only the typed place; the operator can switch suggestions and maps off.

Config.Name: Map Tiles URL
Config.Description: Where the small map of a place is drawn from, with {z}/{x}/{y} in it. Leave blank for the tiles of OpenStreetMap.
